title: The Town Where Borders Go Through Houses
art_style: cute 2D vector sticker illustration, minimalist flat design, chibi proportions, flat colors with no gradients, muted earthy palette, clean dark outline, full body, centered, isolated on a solid plain white background, no text

scenes.narration: In this town, the border between two countries runs right through houses, cafés and shops.
Belgium is here. The Netherlands is here. And this little town is called Baarle.
Baarle is a patchwork. Belgian pieces sit inside the Netherlands, and Dutch pieces sit inside those Belgian pieces.
The border is painted on the ground, with little crosses, so you can see which country you're standing in.
Why so messy? It goes back to the Middle Ages, when local lords swapped and sold tiny plots of farmland.
When Belgium and the Netherlands split in 1830, nobody could agree how to divide it. So they kept every plot as it was.
scenes.tts: When Belgium and the Netherlands split in eighteen thirty, nobody could agree how to divide it. So they kept every plot as it was.

scenes.narration: Some buildings are cut in half. And your address can depend on which side your front door is on.

icons.ai: a cute cartoon wooden front door with a doormat
icons.name: door

scenes.narration: There are two town halls, two police forces, and two sets of rules.
When closing times were different, people would just walk to the other side of a café to keep drinking.
The very last piece of the border was only settled in 1995.
scenes.tts: The very last piece of the border was only settled in nineteen ninety-five.

scenes.narration: So Baarle is one town, two countries, and about thirty borders.
Would you live in a house that's in two countries? Yes or no?
